issue.title: test_agents_row_fit_shares_density_between_gauge_and_bar times out waiting for agent-info-row width
issue.description:
## Flake report

- **Test:** `tests/ace/tui/test_launch_context_bar.py::test_agents_row_fit_shares_density_between_gauge_and_bar`
- **Repro:** `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ace/tui/test_launch_context_bar.py::test_agents_row_fit_shares_density_between_gauge_and_bar -q --tb=line`

`wait_for()` times out after 5.0s because `#agent-info-row.region.width` never becomes > 0.

Observed on 2026-10-04 during restart-wait verification (tool run `980bb79cc98e69e3cefab0bcdfcfe062`, full parallel `just check` after `core-identity-changed` escalation) and again in isolation on the same tree:

- Full parallel check: FAIL (timeout)
- Isolation run 1: FAIL (timeout, 9.1s call)
- Isolation run 2–4 with the restart-wait diff: PASS, FAIL, PASS (fail rate 1/3 in that batch)
- Clean `origin/master` isolation: PASS once

The restart-wait diff does not touch `launch_context_bar` or `AgentInfoRow`. Passing and failing runs share an unchanged tree, so this is intermittent layout/settle rather than a product regression.

task_type_fields.evidence: Full parallel just check failed with wait_for timeout (row.region.width never > 0). Isolation on the same tree: fail, then pass/fail/pass (1/3). Clean origin/master isolation passed once. Restart-wait diff does not touch launch_context_bar.

issue.creation_reason: Discovered during restart-wait just check: the agents-row density test failed under the full parallel lane and then passed and failed on the same tree in isolation.

evidence.note: Reproduced under 'sase tool run check' run 4c482e611c702f4e57eb3c29b94e3444 at master 404b0e2ac2 (escalated full lane, 14 workers, load ~20) by the sase-1eq.5.1 land agent, which changed only the terminology-guard allowlist. This time the node failed with textual.css.query.NoMatches '#frontmatter-raw' on FrontmatterPanel (the sase-1fy stack), not the agent-info-row width timeout. An isolation rerun on the same tree passed. The node evidently flakes through both the layout-settle and FrontmatterPanel.on_mount paths.
